questions.question: A wall is 9 m long and 2.4 m high. What is the wall area?
questions.explanation: Area is found by multiplying length by height. 9 m × 2.4 m = 21.6 m². This calculation helps estimate masonry units and mortar.

questions.category: C2 - Use Drawings, Specifications and Documentation
questions.question: A drawing shows reinforcing steel in a block wall. What should the mason do before building?
options: Ignore it unless the wall is exterior
Confirm bar size, spacing, and location
questions.explanation: Reinforcement must match the drawings and specifications. Size, spacing, and location affect wall strength. Incorrect placement can cause structural problems.

questions.category: D3 - Use Mortars, Grouts and Bonding Agents
questions.question: Why is grout consolidation important in reinforced masonry?
options: It removes voids and helps grout surround reinforcement
questions.explanation: Consolidation helps grout fill cells properly. Voids can reduce bond around reinforcement. Proper grout placement improves wall performance.

questions.category: E2 - Build Load-Bearing Walls and Columns
questions.question: What is the main purpose of a load-bearing masonry wall?
options: To support loads from above and transfer them to the foundation
questions.explanation: Load-bearing walls carry structural loads. They transfer roof, floor, or other loads downward. They must be built exactly to design requirements.

questions.question: What is horizontal masonry commonly associated with?
options: Flat or sloped masonry surfaces such as paving or caps
questions.explanation: Horizontal masonry includes surfaces laid flat or near-flat. Examples can include pavers, caps, and related masonry work. Drainage and level are important considerations.
